files.document_title: North Dakota Pipeline Authority newsletter, volume 6 issue 2, February 2014
files.what_it_shows: Text only, no map. Says WBI Energy announced an open season on January 30, 2014 for the proposed Dakota Pipeline, a 24-inch line to a hub near Emerson, Minnesota, with an initial design of 400 million cubic feet per day.

searched: FERC eLibrary text searches for Dakota Pipeline with WBI, Williston Basin, Moorhead and Viking: no Dakota Pipeline docket exists, so it was never filed with FERC
FERC docket list for later WBI projects (Bakken East PF26-4, North Bakken, Valley Expansion): not this line
Web searches for a WBI or North Dakota Public Service Commission route map: none found
Oil and Gas Journal, Petroleum News, World Pipelines and Natural Gas Intelligence articles from 2013 and 2014: text only, no map
Bakken Shale article and a Wayback lookup: 503 and 429 responses, not retried further
Not checked: North Dakota Public Service Commission and Minnesota Public Utilities Commission dockets, which a February 2014 newsletter says would handle route determination
notes: This was an older WBI proposal from 2013 and 2014, a roughly 375 mile, 24-inch, 400 million cubic feet per day line, open season January 30, 2014, estimated at $650 million. The trade press names the endpoints loosely. Petroleum News says it runs from the Montana-North Dakota state line to the Canadian border in northwestern Minnesota. Oil and Gas Journal says from western North Dakota to northwestern Minnesota. A 2014 company statement quoted in a search result adds a route around Williston from Spring Creek to Tioga and then east to Emerson, Minnesota, on the Canadian border, but that page was not read in full. A May 2013 Oil and Gas Journal item, per the sheet's research notes, instead gives a Viking Gas Transmission interconnection northeast of Moorhead. The two end points disagree, so endpoints-only rests on loose descriptions: western North Dakota near Williston and Spring Creek to northwestern Minnesota near Emerson. No route map was found. The later Bakken East line (docket PF26-4) is a different project that stays in North Dakota.
